pristine_identity.source: Fresh gh release download from chatgptopenaiagi/ARX v4.0.0-b1

verifier.trust_model: The verifier compares exact public artifact names and bytes to SHA256SUMS.txt, validates package/archive structure and metadata, and scans public artifacts for forbidden local/private markers. The GitHub Release is the distribution trust anchor.

cases.method: XOR the final byte of an isolated installer copy.
Truncate an isolated installer copy from 9,297,499 to 4,648,749 bytes.
XOR one byte at the midpoint of an isolated portable ZIP copy.
Change one hexadecimal character in an isolated SHA256SUMS.txt copy without changing artifacts.
Add an unexpected versioned public ZIP to an otherwise pristine copied release directory.
cases.reason: Unexpected or missing versioned public release artifacts.

cases.method: Construct a copied release directory without the required portable ZIP.
Add an unexpected .txt file to an otherwise pristine copied release directory.
cases.reason: The verifier intentionally enumerates versioned public artifact extensions, not arbitrary auxiliary working-directory files.

findings.title: Release-root verifier ignores non-public auxiliary file extensions
findings.evidence: An added UNEXPECTED.txt did not affect verification. In contrast, an unexpected .zip public artifact was rejected.
findings.mitigation: The reviewed GitHub release workflow stages an explicit allowlist of four or five named artifacts before upload (.github/workflows/release-assets.yml:107-125), so arbitrary release-root files are not uploaded by that workflow.
findings.recommendation: For future defense in depth, consider enforcing an exact allowlist over every file in the verification root or ensure every caller first stages only named public artifacts.

findings.title: Checksum integrity is not an independent authenticity mechanism
findings.evidence: The defined tests altered artifacts or the manifest independently and were rejected. Coordinated replacement of both an artifact and an unsigned manifest is outside a bare SHA-256 comparison's threat model.
findings.recommendation: Use human-gated signing and OIDC-backed artifact attestations for future releases; do not retrofit or rewrite Beta 1.

gate.statement: All required copied-artifact mutation, truncation, corruption, manifest, unexpected-public-artifact, and missing-artifact cases were rejected. No published asset was changed.
